To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the QMC model, with its in‐medium hyperfine interaction, can be used to describe a large range of hybrid stars, (2) the model can describe the onset of hyperons in a neutron star, as well as the subsequent stiffening of the equation of state, (3) the model can also describe the onset of a mixed quark‐hadron phase in a neutron star (4) the model can reproduce a large range of neutron star masses and radii

(i) QMC with hyperfine interactions is able to describe simultaneously all available data on the properties of neutron stars, and (ii) QMC with in‐medium hyperfine interactions predicts the appearance of a mixed phase of hadrons and quark matter in neutron stars with masses of the order of $2M_{\odot}$, and that such mixed phase stars have masses in the range $1.9\leq M/M_{\odot}\leq 2.

the QMC model with the in‐medium quark‐quar hyperfine interaction predicts the appearance of a hyperon core in hybrid stars, and that this core is not a quark core, which would be the case if the quark‐meson coupling model were used.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of hybrid stars, QMC is a very promising model for the study of the properties of neutron stars and dense matter in general.
the inclusion of the quark hyperfine interaction leads to a softening of the equation of state (EOS) at high baryon densities, which is in line with the recent observational constraints.
the hyperon incorporation in the QMC model is a necessary step to achieve a consistent description of the nuclear matter properties, but the incorporation of a quark‐core is not.
